Interior Design Quotation Malaysia: Format, Fees & Sample

Published 19 November 2026

An interior design quotation in Malaysia usually has two parts: the design fee, and the design-and-build works grouped by area or trade, with a unit, quantity and rate on every line. Strong quotations also separate provisional sums for items not yet chosen, list loose furniture on its own, and spell out exclusions, a payment schedule and how variations are handled. Below is the format, the common fee models and a sample.

How interior designers in Malaysia charge

Fee model How it works Typical published range
Design fee per sq ft Design and drawings only, priced on the built-up area About RM3–8 per sq ft for homes
Percentage of project cost Fee calculated on the renovation cost Roughly 6–15%, with some guides quoting 10–20%
Design and build Design fee folded into the build price, with a markup on works Varies; often shown as “free design”

Whichever model you use, say it plainly in the quotation. Clients comparing three IDs often can’t tell whether the cheapest quote includes design at all.

Organise by area or by trade?

  • By area (living, kitchen, master bedroom, bathrooms) is easier for homeowners to read and to cut when the budget is tight.
  • By trade (hacking, tiling, carpentry, electrical, painting) is easier for you to cost and for contractors to price.

Many IDs do both: areas as the main sections, with each line naming the trade and specification. For example: “Master bedroom: built-in wardrobe, 8 ft run, plywood carcass, laminate doors, soft-close hinges”.

What to include

  1. Design fee: the model, and what’s included (site measurement, layout, 3D renderings, construction drawings, number of revisions, site supervision).
  2. Build works by area or trade, with unit, quantity, rate and a clear specification on every line.
  3. Provisional sums for items still to be chosen: light fittings, wallpaper, sanitary ware, feature tiles.
  4. Loose furniture and decor, listed separately if you supply them.
  5. Exclusions: appliances, curtains, management deposits, authority fees, whatever isn’t yours.
  6. Validity: how long the prices hold.
  7. Payment schedule linked to design and site milestones.
  8. Terms: variations, defects period, ownership of drawings, and the estimated timeline.

Sample interior design quotation (summary page)

A 1,000 sq ft condo, design and build. The figures are illustrative.

Section Amount (RM)
A. Design fee: layout, 3D, construction drawings, 2 revisions (1,000 sq ft @ RM5) 5,000.00
B. Preliminaries: protection, management permit, site cleaning 1,800.00
C. Living & dining: feature wall, TV console, plaster ceiling, lighting points 18,500.00
D. Kitchen: cabinets, quartz countertop, wall tiles, electrical points 16,200.00
E. Master bedroom: wardrobe, bed headboard panel, ceiling, lighting 14,300.00
F. Bedrooms 2 & 3: wardrobes, study table, lighting 15,600.00
G. Bathrooms ×2: hacking, waterproofing, tiles, screens 26,000.00
H. Painting, whole unit 6,500.00
I. Provisional sums: light fittings RM3,000, wallpaper RM1,200 4,200.00
Total 108,100.00

Each section then has its own detailed page of line items. The summary page is what the client reads first, and it’s where you decide what they’ll compare you on.

Loose furniture, if you supply it, works best as a separate quotation, so the client can approve the renovation without waiting on every sofa choice.

A payment schedule that fits design work

Stage Milestone %
1 Design fee on appointment Design fee
2 Deposit on confirmation of the build quotation 10–20% of build
3 Wet works and electrical completed 30%
4 Carpentry installed 30%
5 Handover Balance, less retention
6 Retention after the defects period About 5%

Homeowner guides treat a 10–20% build deposit as normal and flag anything above 25% upfront as a warning sign. Taking the design fee upfront protects your design time if the client doesn’t go ahead. The renovation payment schedule guide covers payment terms and retention in more detail.

Common interior design quotation mistakes

  • “Free design” with no scope, so the client doesn’t know what they’ll get, or that the fee is in the build price.
  • Lump sums per room (“Master bedroom – RM14,300”) with no breakdown.
  • No provisional sums, so lighting and finishes become surprise costs later.
  • Vague carpentry: no board, finish or hardware spec.
  • No clause on drawings, so the client can take your design to a cheaper contractor.

Changes after approval should go through a variation order. Frequently asked questions

How do interior designers in Malaysia charge?
The common models are a design fee per square foot, a percentage of the renovation cost, or a markup built into the design-and-build price. Guides put design-only fees at roughly RM3 to RM8 per sq ft for homes, and percentage fees anywhere from about 6% to 20% of the project cost, depending on the firm and scope.
What should an interior design quotation include?
The design fee and what it covers, then the build works grouped by area or by trade with a unit, quantity and rate for each line, provisional sums for items not yet chosen, loose furniture and decor separately if you supply them, exclusions, validity, a payment schedule and terms for variations.
Should the design fee be separate from the renovation cost?
Showing it separately is more transparent and protects your design work if the client takes the drawings to another contractor. If you include it in the build price, say so in the quotation, and state that the drawings remain your property until the project is paid for.
What is a provisional sum in an interior design quotation?
A provisional sum is an allowance for an item that hasn't been chosen yet, such as light fittings or a feature wallpaper. The quotation states the allowance, and the final cost is adjusted up or down once the client picks the actual item.
